analysis: Examined base-side units of ClusterOnboardingLive.swift covering lines 1726-2600: readiness wait (waitReady loop, ownWorker incident-log parsing at 1817-1833), lastErrors/errorLines diagnostics, saveDiagnostics redaction (1941-1971, using ClusterDiagnosticRedaction with local identifiers), offeredLine/offeredReadiness/pairLook/pairServing (2169-2284), the login subprocess (2302-2310), test requests, leaderStatus/publishStep, localStatus, and localStop (2546-2591). Changed base ranges in these units are 2217, 2223-2224, 2286-2289, 2360-2361, 2519, 2546-2547, 2552, 2557-2563. The patch excerpt (head 77-78, 399-408, 464-465) shows a new stopsAsked counter carried in status replies and serve(unlessStoppedSince:) gating serve on forwarded stopsBefore, i.e. a race fix so a forwarded serve does not override a later person-requested stop. Head-side text for the stop/serve changes (head 2238-2240, 2377-2379, 2409-2415, 2542-2587) is not in this batch, so the new localStop/stop-counter logic could not be verified directly. The peer over the cable is a co-owned Mac in the same cluster; these paths are local onboarding UX and stop ordering, not coordinator/consumer trust boundaries (TB-002, TB-011) or prompt data (A-001). No cryptographic, attestation, App Attest authorization (A-016) or cache (T-041) logic changes are visible. Integration should confirm in head source that: stopsAsked is monotonic and persisted in the store record, a stale/forged stopsBefore from the peer can only suppress a serve (fail toward stopped), localStop still drains the local part before asking the peer (memory-retirement ordering), and pair-stop detection (pairStopped at base 2288) still ends waits. No regression identified from supplied evidence.
